title: Massina Empire
capsule: The Massina Empire (also called the Caliphate of Hamdullahi) was a Fulani theocratic state in the inner Niger Delta of present-day Mali, founded by Seku Amadu in 1818 following his victory over Bambara forces at the Battle of Noukouma, which he interpreted as divine sanction for a jihad to impose Maliki Islamic law across the region. Amadu built a sophisticated governance structure with a 40-member Grand Council, a state educational system for both sexes, and a network of mosques and madrasas throughout the Niger bend, making it one of the most organized theocratic polities of nineteenth-century sub-Saharan Africa. The empire collapsed in 1862 when Umar Tall of the Toucouleur Empire invaded with overwhelming force; the third and last Amadu, considered too weak a ruler, was captured and executed, and the capital Hamdullahi was leveled.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The empire's core territory in the Niger Delta and inner bend is well established; its northern and eastern tributary zones are less precisely mapped in modern scholarship.
